security_audit.summary: Community skill of Markdown documentation (9 files, 975 lines) for configuring Prisma ORM across database providers. All 178 static findings adjudicated as false positives: they are standard, documented Prisma patterns — the '../generated' client output path (flagged as path traversal), env("DATABASE_URL")/process.env.DATABASE_URL datasource config (flagged as connection-string and environment access), example URLs and .env instructions, and Markdown code-fence backticks (flagged as shell execution). No executable payloads, network exfiltration, or prompt-injection content were found. No net-new semantic risks identified.

content.user_title: Configure Prisma With Any Database Provider
content.value_statement: Setting up Prisma for a new database means juggling datasource config, driver adapters, and connection strings that differ by provider. This skill gives Claude provider-specific, step-by-step guides so it configures PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, SQL Server, or CockroachDB correctly the first time.
actual_capabilities: Guides Prisma configuration for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, SQL Server, and CockroachDB.
Selects the correct driver adapter and JavaScript driver for each SQL database.
Shows how to define the datasource and generator blocks in schema.prisma.
Explains connection string format and where to store DATABASE_URL for each provider.
Walks through installing Prisma CLI and Prisma Client, then generating the client.
Flags provider-specific rules, such as keeping MongoDB projects on Prisma 6.x.
limitations: Provides configuration guidance only; it does not run migrations or connect to a live database.
Covers the listed database providers and does not include every third-party adapter.
Does not manage secrets or provision database servers for you.
Assumes a Node.js and TypeScript project that meets the stated version prerequisites.

use_cases.title: Start a new Prisma project
use_cases.description: A developer initializing a project gets the correct schema, adapter, and client setup for their chosen database.

use_cases.title: Switch database providers
use_cases.description: A team migrating from one database to another follows provider-specific rules to update the datasource and adapter.

use_cases.title: Fix connection issues
use_cases.description: An engineer troubleshooting a failed connection checks the connection string format and environment variable setup for their provider.

prompt_templates.title: Basic PostgreSQL setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Prisma with a PostgreSQL database in my project.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner starting a new project with the default provider.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the right adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: I am using MySQL with Prisma 7. Which driver adapter and driver should I install, and how do I wire them into Prisma Client?
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer who needs the correct adapter for a SQL provider.

prompt_templates.title: MongoDB configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Prisma for a MongoDB database and tell me which Prisma version to use.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer setting up a document database with provider-specific rules.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a connection failure
prompt_templates.prompt: My Prisma app cannot connect to SQL Server. Review my connection string format and environment variable setup and tell me what is wrong.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user debugging a production connection problem.

output_examples.input: Set up Prisma with a PostgreSQL database.
output_examples.output: Claude explains the steps: install Prisma CLI and Prisma Client, add a datasource block with the postgresql provider, add a generator block with an output path, install the pg driver and the @prisma/adapter-pg adapter, set DATABASE_URL in your .env file, then run prisma generate and instantiate Prisma Client with the PostgreSQL adapter.

output_examples.input: Which adapter do I need for SQLite?
output_examples.output: Claude recommends the @prisma/adapter-better-sqlite3 adapter with the better-sqlite3 driver for a local SQLite file, or the @prisma/adapter-libsql adapter with @libsql/client when using Turso or LibSQL, and shows how to pass the adapter to Prisma Client.

output_examples.input: How should I set up MongoDB with Prisma?
output_examples.output: Claude advises staying on the latest Prisma 6.x release for MongoDB, keeping url = env("DATABASE_URL") in schema.prisma, using the mongodb provider, and not applying the SQL driver-adapter workflow.

best_practices: Store the connection string in DATABASE_URL through an environment file rather than hardcoding it in the schema.
Run prisma generate after every change to the schema so the generated client stays in sync.
Match the driver adapter and JavaScript driver to your specific database provider.
anti_patterns: Applying the SQL driver-adapter workflow to a MongoDB project instead of the MongoDB-specific setup.
Committing a real connection string or password into schema.prisma or version control.
Skipping client regeneration after editing the schema, which leaves stale generated types.

faq.question: Which database providers does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, SQL Server, and CockroachDB, plus Prisma Postgres.

faq.question: Do I need a driver adapter for every database?
faq.answer: SQL databases use a driver adapter in the standard Prisma 7 workflow. MongoDB uses the classic setup and does not use a SQL adapter.

faq.question: Where should I put my connection string?
faq.answer: Place it in an environment variable named DATABASE_URL, usually inside a local .env file, and reference it from the configuration.

faq.question: Why does the guide keep MongoDB on Prisma 6.x?
faq.answer: The MongoDB workflow differs from the SQL adapter workflow. Prisma 6.x keeps the connection URL in the schema and remains the supported path for MongoDB projects.

faq.question: What versions of Node.js and TypeScript are required?
faq.answer: The guide expects Node.js 20.19.0 or newer and TypeScript 5.4.0 or newer.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to my database or run migrations?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration guidance only. You still run the Prisma CLI commands and manage your own database.
